claims.text: Post-process deep cryogenic treatment can improve the dimensional precision of LMD-fabricated high-entropy-alloy components.
Post-process deep cryogenic treatment can improve the mechanical integrity of LMD-fabricated high-entropy-alloy components.
Post-process deep cryogenic treatment can reduce fabrication-induced defects in LMD-fabricated high-entropy alloys.
As-deposited LMD high-entropy-alloy components contain accumulated thermal or residual stress.
As-deposited LMD high-entropy-alloy components exhibit thermal gradients and fabrication-induced defects.
DCT is applied after LMD fabrication as a post-processing treatment.
An effective DCT procedure consists of immersion in liquid nitrogen at approximately -196 °C for 24–48 hours under ambient pressure.
DCT reduces internal residual stresses in LMD-fabricated high-entropy alloys.
DCT induces microstructural phase transitions without requiring additional deformation.
DCT refines the microstructure of LMD-fabricated high-entropy alloys.
DCT increases lattice distortion in the treated alloy.
Uniform thermal contraction and induced phase transformations relieve internal stresses.
The DCT-induced changes reduce defect formation and produce a more homogeneous microstructure.
A more homogeneous microstructure improves dimensional stability and mechanical properties.
Relative to the as-deposited baseline, DCT will increase tensile strength by roughly 11–25%.
DCT will reduce porosity and overall defect density relative to the as-deposited baseline.
DCT is expected to be effective for BCC high-entropy alloys processed by LMD.
The effect of DCT may vary with alloy system, LMD processing parameters, and cryogenic soak duration.

contradictions.description: The intervention is explicitly applied after fabrication, but the mechanism says it reduces defect formation. A post-fabrication treatment could potentially heal or reduce existing defects, but it cannot prevent defects that already formed during deposition without an additional explanation.
